reconstructed_theorem_text: Let X be an arbitrary type, let L : (X → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] (X → ℝ) be a real-linear generator, and let α ∈ ℝ with α > 0. Suppose that for every g : X → ℝ and every y ∈ X, α Γ_L(g,g)(y) ≤ (1/2)(L(Γ_L(g,g))(y) - Γ_L(g,Lg)(y) - Γ_L(g,Lg)(y)). Then, for every f : X → ℝ and every x ∈ X, 2α Γ_L(f,f)(x) ≤ L(Γ_L(f,f))(x) - 2Γ_L(f,Lf)(x).
objects: An arbitrary type X; a real-linear generator L on all real-valued functions X → ℝ; a positive real parameter α; a universally quantified curvature-test function g and point y; and the conclusion's function f and point x; together with the binary carré-du-champ expression Γ_L.
domains: X is an arbitrary type. L : (X → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] (X → ℝ). The parameter α is real. The functions g and f map X to ℝ, the points y and x lie in X, and all values, products, differences, and inequalities displayed are real-valued.
quantifiers: For every arbitrary type X, every real-linear generator L, and every α ∈ ℝ satisfying α > 0: if the expanded curvature inequality holds for every g : X → ℝ and every y ∈ X, then the stated lower bound holds for every f : X → ℝ and every x ∈ X.
assumptions: First, 0 < α. Second, for all g : X → ℝ and y ∈ X, αΓ_L(g,g)(y) ≤ (1/2)(L(Γ_L(g,g))(y) - Γ_L(g,Lg)(y) - Γ_L(g,Lg)(y)). No further assumption on L, Γ_L, g, f, x, or y is present.
conclusion: For every f : X → ℝ and x ∈ X, 2αΓ_L(f,f)(x) ≤ L(Γ_L(f,f))(x) - 2Γ_L(f,Lf)(x).
scopes: The curvature premise is global over all real-valued functions g and all points y of X. The conclusion is pointwise for an arbitrary real-valued f at an arbitrary x. The positivity hypothesis on α is explicit even though the displayed conclusion is the direct doubled form of the curvature inequality.
constant_dependencies: The premise uses the exact scalar (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ = 1/2 and contains two separate identical subtractions of Γ_L(g,Lg)(y). Doubling yields exactly 2α on the left and exactly -2Γ_L(f,Lf)(x) on the right, with no additional constants.
